topics.title: Lighting and clarity
topics.text: Use even lighting so the balls and rails are easy to distinguish. Avoid strong reflections, deep shadows, or motion blur. A clear photograph makes it easier to review the detected positions.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Reviewing the table boundaries
topics.text: Before working with individual balls, check that the table boundaries in the image match the actual playing surface. If the alignment looks wrong, correct the available table reference points before transferring the layout.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Understanding perspective
topics.text: A camera photograph can make the far end of the table appear narrower than the near end. The analysis process uses table geometry to translate image positions into a top-down practice layout. Review the result and lets you adjust the alignment as needed.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Detecting visible balls
topics.text:
After loading an image, examine the balls identified by the analysis. Compare each detected position with the image and look for any missed balls or markers that do not belong.

Once the visible balls are assigned, compare their numbers and positions with the original image. Take a moment to verify the cue ball and the intended target ball before planning your shot.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Assigning ball identities
topics.text: A detected ball may initially be labeled Unassigned. Select that ball and choose its correct identity. Use the image as your reference, and repeat until the balls needed for your practice layout are identified.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Recognizing the cue ball
topics.text: Identify the cue ball carefully. Its location determines the starting point for every planned shot, so verify its position and identity before studying the aiming guides.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Correcting a ball position
topics.text: If a detected ball is slightly out of place, adjust its position to match the image. Small placement errors can change the cut angle, contact point, and predicted path.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Handling missed detections
topics.text: If a ball visible in the image was not detected, use the available editing controls to add it to the layout. Position it by comparing nearby rails, diamonds, and other balls.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Handling false detections
topics.text: If the analysis identifies something that is not a ball, remove that incorrect detection using the available editing controls. Check the image again to make sure the remaining layout represents the real table.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Checking ball numbers
topics.text: Once the visible balls are assigned, compare their numbers and positions with the original image. Take a moment to verify the cue ball and the intended target ball before planning your shot.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Transferring the arrangement
topics.text: When the image arrangement looks correct, use the available control to bring it into the trainer table. Check the transferred positions before you begin aiming or adjusting shot settings.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Comparing image and table
topics.text: Compare the practice layout with the source image. Pay special attention to balls near cushions, clustered balls, and narrow gaps. Correct any differences that could change the shot you want to study.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Planning a shot from an image
topics.text: With the transferred layout on the trainer table, choose the cue ball and your intended target. Use the aiming and geometry guides to explore the contact point and possible cue-ball route before selecting Execute Shot.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Reviewing ball positions in the image
topics.text: Review the transferred ball positions before practicing. If a ball is partly hidden, close to a cushion, or difficult to identify in the image, adjust its position or identity to match the image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Aligning a photographed table
topics.text: After selecting Choose Image, try Corner Sensing. If the corners are misplaced, set them manually by matching the highlighted diagram points: pocket 1, then pocket 3, pocket 4, and pocket 6. The first two points follow one long rail in either portrait or landscape. The last side connects back to pocket 1. This keeps the photograph aligned with the trainer’s pocket numbering. Use Reset Corners if you need to start over.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Rack selection and ball analysis
topics.text: Choose the appropriate rack setting, or leave it on Auto. Select Analyze Balls to identify balls in the photograph. Review the results and use the identity dropdowns to correct any numbers.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Reviewing identity suggestions
topics.text: Detected-ball cards may show suggested identities and confidence indicators. Compare those suggestions with the photograph, then choose the correct identity from the dropdown.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Adding or removing a detection
topics.text: If a ball was missed, select Add Missed Ball and click or touch its center in the photograph. Assign the ball identity afterward. If an incorrect detection appears, use Delete to remove it.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Inspecting the photograph
topics.text: Zoom into the image to inspect positions and ball numbers. Move around the enlarged view to examine different parts of the table, then return to the full view before finishing your arrangement.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Saved image controls
topics.text: Use Saved Images to return to a photograph you worked with before. Select an image and choose Open. The nearby controls also let you remove a saved image or save and download the current image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Applying a photographed layout
topics.text: When the ball identities and positions are correct, choose Apply to Trainer Table to transfer the arrangement. To keep it for future practice, enter a layout name and select Apply + Save Layout.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: AI detection mode
topics.text: The AI button enables or disables the trained ball detector. Ready means the models are loaded. Auto or Loading means they are preparing. Retry restarts a failed load. With AI off, Analyze Balls uses the original detector. Review the detected identities and positions before applying your layout.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Open Analyze Get Started
topics.text: Open the Analyze Get Started walkthrough. It guides you from choosing a image through calibration, detection, review, transfer, saving, and sharing. Audio starts with the first file and stops after the last. Select the launcher again to close it.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Analyze Explorer mode
topics.text: Turn Explorer on to select a image-analysis control or area and hear what it does. Turn Explorer off when you want to edit the image, corners, or detected balls.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Close Analyze page
topics.text: Close Analyze and return to the trainer table. Use Apply to Trainer Table first if you want to transfer the reviewed ball arrangement.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Choose image
topics.text: Choose an image from this device. Portrait and landscape images keep their original proportions. Identify the head or kitchen end and the foot or rack end of the table. Then select Find / Add Corners to match the numbered reference points in the table diagram to your image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Corner sensing
topics.text: Corner Sensing estimates the four inside playing-surface corners in a full-table image. It orders them along the table’s long direction, including portrait images. Check the numbered diagram against the image and confirm the head and foot ends. Drag a marker to correct its position. If the orientation is wrong, select Reset Corners and use Find / Add Corners to mark the references yourself. For a partial table, choose its coverage in Custom Table Layouts and mark the highlighted points manually.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Custom Table Layouts
topics.text: Custom Table Layouts opens the table-region and alignment controls beside your image. The diagram follows the image’s estimated orientation. Use the Head / Kitchen End menu to choose its direction, or Flip Ends if the head and foot ends are reversed. Choose the coverage you can see and match the numbered references. Analyze Balls closes this panel so the right side shows the detected balls. Select Custom Table Layouts to open it again.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Reset corners
topics.text: Reset Corners clears the marked corners and their alignment references. Select Find / Add Corners to start marking again. Follow the highlighted numbered points in the table diagram, rather than the corners of your screen. For partial coverage, use the matching region boundaries, which may be diamond intersections instead of pockets.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Choose analysis rack type
topics.text: Choose Auto, Eight Ball, Nine Ball, Ten Ball, or Custom before analyzing. The selected rack type helps determine which ball identities are allowed. Custom permits any supported ball arrangement.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Analyze Balls
topics.text: Analyze Balls detects ball candidates inside the calibrated table region. Custom Table Layouts closes so you can review the detected balls on the right. Check each candidate and assign its identity before applying the layout to the Trainer.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Add Missed Ball
topics.text: Select Add Missed Ball, then tap the center of one ball the detector missed. The tool turns off automatically after placing that ball. Assign its identity in the review list. Select Add Missed Ball again whenever you need to add another.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: AI detector mode and readiness
topics.text: This control selects the trained ball detector and shows its readiness. Loading means the model is being prepared. Ready means it can be used. Off uses the alternative detector, and Retry attempts to load the model again.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Choose saved photo
topics.text: Choose a image previously saved in this device's browser. Selection alone does not open it.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Open saved photo
topics.text: Open the image chosen in the saved-image menu for inspection and analysis.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Remove saved photo
topics.text: Remove the selected image from this device's saved-image archive.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Save photo in browser
topics.text: Save the current image in this device's browser image archive.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Download photo image
topics.text: Download the current image as an image file.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Choose photo section
topics.text: Choose Full Table, Head/Kitchen, Foot/Rack, or Custom. Use fixed pocket numbering P1 clockwise to P6.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Set section coverage
topics.text: Set how many diamond intervals are visible from the selected end of the table. This locates a quarter, half, or larger image region on the trainer. Full Table and Custom use their own boundaries, so this slider is disabled for those choices.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Set custom left boundary
topics.text: Move the left vertical boundary of the custom region using its slider or diagram line. Match a visible rail or diamond position. Boundaries snap to half-diamond intervals, and changing the region requires corner calibration again.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Set custom right boundary
topics.text: Move the custom region's right vertical boundary by slider or dragging its diagram line.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Set custom top boundary
topics.text: Move the custom region's top horizontal boundary by slider or dragging its diagram line, using half-diamond reference spacing.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Set custom bottom boundary
topics.text: Move the custom region's bottom horizontal boundary by slider or dragging its diagram line, using half-diamond reference spacing.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Refine Alignment or Done Refining
topics.text: After four corners, start diamond refinement. Choose a reference on the diagram and then its matching point in the image. Add more references and finish with Done Refining.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Clear refinement diamonds
topics.text: Remove the extra diamond refinement references while retaining the basic corner calibration. Recheck alignment afterward.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Pan photo left and right
topics.text: When zoomed in, drag the bottom bar or use the mouse wheel over it to move horizontally without changing zoom.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Pan photo up and down
topics.text: When zoomed in, drag the side bar or use the mouse wheel over it to move vertically without changing zoom.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Name analyzed table layout
topics.text: Enter the name used when saving or downloading this analyzed arrangement.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Load shared table file into Analyze
topics.text: Open a trainer JSON file from local storage. It appears as a staged layout with its name and balls; review it, then Apply or Apply + Save.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Save analyzed layout JSON file
topics.text: Download the assigned ball arrangement as a portable table JSON file for an instructor or student. Unassigned entries are excluded.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Apply to Trainer Table
topics.text: Transfer the reviewed assigned balls to the main trainer table.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Apply and Save Layout
topics.text: Transfer the reviewed arrangement to the trainer and save it as a named browser layout.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Zoom photo with mouse wheel
topics.text: Hover over the image and use the wheel to zoom around the pointer while retaining image proportions.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Drag zoomed photo to pan
topics.text: Hold and drag a zoomed image to see another section.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Mark four corner references
topics.text: Use the numbered table diagram to guide your four taps. For a full table, begin at the head-end corner shown as pocket one. The second point is at the other end of that same long rail, pocket three. Cross the foot-end short rail to pocket four, then return along the other long rail to pocket six. Match these physical references wherever they appear in your image. Do not use a fixed top-left, top-right screen order. For partial coverage, follow the four highlighted region points instead.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Adjust marked photo corner
topics.text: Drag a marked corner to the exact cloth or chosen diamond intersection.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Calibration orientation diagram
topics.text: This shows fixed P1 clockwise to P6, six numbered rail sections, head/kitchen left, foot/rack right, and highlighted coverage.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Select diamond reference on diagram
topics.text: Select a visible rail diamond or pocket reference in Refine Alignment, then mark its matching location in the image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Place matching diamond in photo
topics.text: With a diagram reference selected, tap its precise corresponding image position.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Alignment fit and reference count
topics.text: This shows the marked-reference count and image-pixel fit readout; inspect alignment if a reference is placed incorrectly.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Photo diamond grid overlay
topics.text: This shows the faint horizontal, vertical, and half-diamond guides used to compare real ball positions.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Photo head and kitchen overlay
topics.text: This shows the faint head/kitchen reference and the break side of the table.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Photo foot and rack overlay
topics.text: This shows the faint triangle, foot/rack end, and rack position.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Detected and assigned ball counts
topics.text: This shows total detected candidates, assigned balls, and entries still needing review.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Assigned ball summary icon
topics.text: Select a numbered summary icon to locate its corresponding ball in the image and review list.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Cue ball summary icon
topics.text: Locate the assigned cue ball from its summary icon above the end of the solids row.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Unassigned question mark icon
topics.text: Select a question-mark icon to jump to that candidate for assignment or deletion.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Detected ball marker in photo
topics.text: Tap a numbered transparent marker to focus its review row.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Question mark in photo
topics.text: Tap an unassigned marker to review the candidate. Assign a real ball or delete a false detection.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Detected ball photograph crop
topics.text: Use the actual cropped image to compare the candidate with the table and its selected identity.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Assign detected ball identity
topics.text: Choose Cue Ball, ball 1 through 15, or Unassigned.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Delete detected candidate
topics.text: Remove this candidate from the review list and its marker from the image, without deleting the original image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Most likely identity suggestions
topics.text: These suggestions rank the likely ball identities for this candidate. Compare them with the image crop, then choose the correct identity yourself.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Detection confidence and warnings
topics.text: Confidence indicates how strongly the detector supports an identity. Review close calls, duplicate warnings, and rack-rule adjustments alongside the image crop before assigning the ball.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Correct detected ball position
topics.text: Drag a detected ball center in the image to correct its mapped position.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Place missed ball in photo
topics.text: Tap the center of the one missed ball you want to add. After that entry is placed, adding turns off automatically. Assign the ball’s identity in the review list. To add another ball, select Add Missed Ball again.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Analysis status message
topics.text: This shows the current analysis or calibration status and the next action requested.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Solids summary row
topics.text: The solids row shows balls one through eight in order. Select a visible ball icon to find its corresponding image marker and review entry.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Stripes summary row
topics.text: The stripes row shows balls nine through fifteen in order, below the solids. Select a visible icon to find and edit that ball in the review list.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Unassigned review row
topics.text: Question marks below the stripes represent candidates that still need identification. Select one to reach its review entry, assign a ball number, or delete a false detection.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Pocket 1 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Pocket 1 is the top-left corner of the full-table diagram. Numbering stays fixed as coverage changes. Use it as a calibration reference when it is visible in your image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Pocket 2 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Pocket 2 is the top middle side pocket of the full-table diagram. Numbering stays fixed as coverage changes. Use it as a calibration reference when it is visible in your image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Pocket 3 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Pocket 3 is the top-right corner of the full-table diagram. Numbering stays fixed as coverage changes. Use it as a calibration reference when it is visible in your image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Pocket 4 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Pocket 4 is the bottom-right corner of the full-table diagram. Numbering stays fixed as coverage changes. Use it as a calibration reference when it is visible in your image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Pocket 5 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Pocket 5 is the bottom middle side pocket of the full-table diagram. Numbering stays fixed as coverage changes. Use it as a calibration reference when it is visible in your image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Pocket 6 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Pocket 6 is the bottom-left corner of the full-table diagram. Numbering stays fixed as coverage changes. Use it as a calibration reference when it is visible in your image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Rail 1 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Rail 1 is the cushion section between pockets 1 and 2. Its diamonds provide distance references for table orientation and image alignment.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Rail 2 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Rail 2 is the cushion section between pockets 2 and 3. Its diamonds provide distance references for table orientation and image alignment.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Rail 3 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Rail 3 is the cushion section between pockets 3 and 4. Its diamonds provide distance references for table orientation and image alignment.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Rail 4 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Rail 4 is the cushion section between pockets 4 and 5. Its diamonds provide distance references for table orientation and image alignment.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Rail 5 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Rail 5 is the cushion section between pockets 5 and 6. Its diamonds provide distance references for table orientation and image alignment.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Rail 6 in calibration diagram
topics.text: Rail 6 is the cushion section between pockets 6 and 1. Its diamonds provide distance references for table orientation and image alignment.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Choose locally saved JSON file
topics.text: Browse the named table and session JSON copies saved or added in this device browser. Selection alone does not load the file.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Load Saved JSON file
topics.text: Stage the selected file on Analyze for review before applying it.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Add Files to saved JSON list
topics.text: Select one or more trainer JSON downloads to add to this device browser saved-file list.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Refresh connected folder JSON list
topics.text: Scan the connected auto-save folder for trainer JSON files. If no folder is connected, choose one. Supported browsers only.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Saved file storage message
topics.text: This shows that the list contains browser copies plus files added or scanned from a connected folder. Files do not transfer automatically to another device.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Previous audio file or lesson
topics.text: Skip back to the previous file in this lesson, or to the previous lesson.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Stop audio
topics.text: Stop the current narration and reset its playback position.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Play or pause audio
topics.text: Start or pause the selected narration.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Rewind audio ten seconds
topics.text: Move ten seconds backward within the current audio file without switching lessons.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Forward audio ten seconds
topics.text: Move ten seconds forward within the current audio file without switching lessons.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Next audio file or lesson
topics.text: Skip to the next file within the lesson, or the next lesson.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Autoplay next lesson
topics.text: Turn automatic progression on or off. Get Started opens with this enabled, plays from the first file, and stops after the last.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Read narration text
topics.text: Open or close the selected lesson transcript beneath the compact controls.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: More lesson resources
topics.text: Open or close resources for the selected lesson.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Reset Guide session
topics.text: Reset the Guide state after confirmation.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Open or close reading area
topics.text: Expand or collapse the transcript/resource area while keeping the compact lesson controls visible.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Choose audio lesson
topics.text: Select a named lesson from the compact menu.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Full table photo coverage
topics.text: Use all four real table corners for a full-table image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Head or kitchen photo coverage
topics.text: Use the left/head portion of the fixed trainer orientation and select its diamond extent.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Foot or rack photo coverage
topics.text: Use the right/foot portion of the fixed trainer orientation and select its diamond extent.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Custom middle or quarter photo coverage
topics.text: Define a middle band or quarter area with four boundaries.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Analyze rack — Rack: Auto
topics.text: Auto infers the likely game arrangement from the detected balls. Review its assignments, or choose a specific rack type when you know which game is shown.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Analyze rack — 9-Ball
topics.text: Nine Ball limits the expected numbered balls to one through nine, together with the cue ball.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Analyze rack — 10-Ball
topics.text: Ten Ball limits the expected numbered balls to one through ten, together with the cue ball.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Analyze rack — 8-Ball
topics.text: Eight Ball expects the cue ball and balls one through fifteen, including solids, stripes, and the eight.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Analyze rack — Custom
topics.text: Custom allows a practice layout without restricting it to a particular game rack. Review and assign the balls visible in the image.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Assign Cue Ball
topics.text: Assign this candidate as the cue ball. Its summary icon moves to the cue-ball position above the end of the solids row. If another entry already has that identity, it returns to review. Assigned balls can be transferred to the trainer.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Assign numbered ball
topics.text: Choose the number shown on this object ball. Its summary icon moves into the matching solid or stripe position. If the number is already assigned elsewhere, the previous entry returns to review. Assigned balls can be transferred to the trainer.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Leave candidate Unassigned
topics.text: Leave this candidate unassigned when you still need to inspect it. It remains a question mark in the image and the review summary. Unassigned candidates are excluded when you apply the layout to the trainer.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Image and camera heading
topics.text: This area is where you choose the image to analyze. Use Choose Image to open a picture from your device.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Table setup
topics.text: Table Setup groups Find / Add Corners, Reset Corners, Custom Table Layouts, and Corner Sensing, followed by rack choice and ball-analysis controls. Mark the table region and review its alignment before analyzing the balls.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Saved images heading
topics.text: Saved Images contains images stored in this device browser. It is separate from Saved Files, which contains table and session JSON layouts.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Find / Add Corners
topics.text: Find / Add Corners opens the numbered table diagram for manual marking. Match the highlighted reference to the same point in your image and tap it. Continue through all four references. Portrait and landscape images use the same table references, even though they appear in different places on the screen. If four corners are already marked, drag their markers to adjust them, or use Reset Corners to start again.
topics.layoutReason: Contextual control explanation; preserve current table.

topics.title: Set the table corners
topics.text: After choosing an image, select Find / Add Corners. The small table diagram highlights the next point to mark. Match that point to the same physical corner or boundary in your image. For a full table, start at the head-end corner shown as pocket one. Follow the same long rail to pocket three at the foot end. Cross the foot-end short rail to pocket four, then return along the other long rail to pocket six. This table-based order works for portrait and landscape images; the first two points follow a long rail, rather than the top edge of the screen. Use Reset Corners if you need to begin again. Use Custom Table Layouts for partial coverage and diamond references. Corner Sensing can estimate a full-table outline, but check its numbered orientation before continuing. Once the outline matches, select Analyze Balls.

topics.title: Head / Kitchen End
topics.text: The Head / Kitchen End menu controls how the table diagram matches your image. Auto estimates portrait or landscape orientation from the image and corner outline. It cannot identify the actual head end from the cloth alone. Choose Top or Bottom for a vertical table, or Left or Right for a horizontal table. Match the head, break, and kitchen end to the real table. Changing orientation clears the previous ball analysis so you can check the corners and analyze again.

topics.title: Flip Ends
topics.text: Flip Ends swaps the head and foot ends of the table diagram. Use it when the head, break, or kitchen end is shown at the opposite end from your image. Existing corner positions stay in place, but their numbered table references change. Review the alignment and select Analyze Balls again.

topics.text: Tap Choose Image to begin. You can also open a saved image, load a saved table file, or use the current image. Back revisits a step. Next confirms choices. The walkthrough waits for required actions.

topics.title: Walkthrough: Select and open
topics.text: Select your image and choose Open in the device window. For a saved image, select its name and tap Open. For a table file, select the file and open it. We will continue when it has loaded.

topics.title: Walkthrough: Open corner setup
topics.text: Your image is loaded. Tap Find / Add Corners to open the table diagram. For a partial table image, choose the matching coverage in Custom Table Layouts before marking the corners.

topics.title: Walkthrough: Identify four corners
topics.text: Match each highlighted numbered reference on the diagram to the inside cushion edge in your image. Notice the orientation: Top or Bottom is portrait; Left or Right is landscape. For a full table in Auto, pocket one becomes top right in portrait and top left in landscape. Corner Sensing can estimate a full-table outline. Check all four markers.

topics.title: Walkthrough: Confirm orientation
topics.text: Check the head, break, and kitchen end against your image. Choose Top or Bottom for portrait, or Left or Right for landscape. Use Flip Ends if reversed. Check the foot spot message and the four numbered markers. Tap Next when the orientation and alignment are correct.

topics.title: Walkthrough: Confirm rack type
topics.text: Leave Rack on Auto, or select the game shown in your image. Use Custom for a drill or an unusual arrangement. Select a different rack type, or tap Next to keep the current choice.

topics.title: Walkthrough: Analyze the balls
topics.text: Tap Analyze Balls. The walkthrough waits for analysis to finish. AI Ready shows the detector status; if the trained detector is unavailable, the app can use its local fallback.

topics.title: Walkthrough: Review every ball
topics.text: Check every ball number and position. Tap an image marker or ball icon to find its review entry. Correct identities and delete false detections. Add Missed Ball places one ball per activation. Zoom and pan to check closely. Tap Next when all remaining balls have unique identities and the layout looks right.

topics.title: Walkthrough: Keep an image or file?
topics.text: Saving here is optional. Save Image keeps the image on this device. Download saves an image copy. Save Table File downloads a shareable layout. These are separate from saving a named Trainer layout. Choose any you want, then tap Next, or simply tap Next to skip.

topics.title: Walkthrough: Send the layout to Trainer
topics.text: Choose Apply to Trainer Table to practice now. Or enter a layout name and choose Apply plus Save Layout to keep it for reuse on this device. The walkthrough finishes only after the layout is successfully applied.
